front.title: Extract fixture: nish/hex without a byte-list vector

abstract.t: Status: proposed. Module: std/hex.ts (nish/hex). A hexadecimal codec for nish: hexEncode writes lowercase hex, and hexDecode reads hex in any case and refuses everything else with null.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
Nish has no public hex codec, and 38 test files define their own. This spec adds one, for tests, test vectors and configuration that carries keys in hex.

section.name: Interface
Length
section.t: hexEncode MUST return exactly two characters per input byte.
section.sourcecode: // P-ENC-LEN covers R-ENC-LEN — two characters per byte forall (b: u8[] /* 0..64 */) => hexEncode(b).length === 2 * b.length

section.name: Digits
section.t: Each byte MUST be written high nibble first, using the digits 0-9 and a-f.
hexEncode MUST NOT emit uppercase digits, separators or a prefix.

section.name: Accepted input
section.t: hexDecode MUST accept the digits 0-9, a-f and A-F, in any mix of case.

section.name: Rejected input
section.t: hexDecode MUST return null when the text has an odd length or contains any other character, including whitespace and a "0x" prefix.
section.sourcecode: // P-OTHER covers R-DEC-REJECT — any other character, anywhere in an even-length text, is refused forall ( a: string /* 0..16 hexdigit HEXDIGIT */, x: string /* 1..1 " \t\n\r!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@GHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~" */, z: string /* 0..16 hexdigit HEXDIGIT */, ) => hexDecode(a + (x + z)) === null where (a + (x + z)).length % 2 === 0

// P-OTHER-EDGE covers R-DEC-REJECT — the characters next to each digit range are refused forall ( a: string /* 0..16 hexdigit HEXDIGIT */, x: string /* 1..1 "/:@G`g" */, z: string /* 0..16 hexdigit HEXDIGIT */, ) => hexDecode(a + (x + z)) === null where (a + (x + z)).length % 2 === 0

section.name: Empty input
section.t: hexDecode of the empty string MUST return an empty array, not null.

section.name: Round trip
section.t: For all bytes b, hexDecode(hexEncode(b)) MUST equal b.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Test vectors and configuration decoded by this module are often key material.
hexDecode MUST NOT index a table by the value of a digit, so that its running time depends only on the length of its input.

Untested: A constraint on how hexDecode is written and on its timing, not on what it returns: no functional test observes a table lookup or a data-dependent running time. Review the implementation for it.

tr.td: RFC 4648 §10: BASE16("") = "" decodes to the empty array
an odd length is refused with null
a "0x" prefix is refused with null

front.title: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings

abstract.t: This document describes the commonly used base 64, base 32, and base 16 encoding schemes. It also discusses the use of line-feeds in encoded data, use of padding in encoded data, use of non-alphabet characters in encoded data, use of different encoding alphabets, and canonical encodings. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
